comments.author: @TravelBeyond4K
comments.text: What strikes me most in this compilation is how humans keep building homes where nature makes it hardest—from underground towns in Coober Pedy escaping 50°C heat and Grindavik sitting on lava fields, to sulfur miners hauling up to 90 kg at Kawah Ijen and ghost towns like Kolmanskop being reclaimed by sand. It shows both human stubbornness and how fragile our footprint can be. Which of these places would you never dare to call home?
